text: To illustrate historical trends, Figure ES-2 shows U.S. production of PV components between 2007 and 2024. The U.S. Department of Commerce determined that the steep drop in U.S. module production between 2011 and 2012 was due to competition from low-price Chinese modules (U.S. Federal Register 2011). Beginning in 2012, the United States enacted a series of trade barriers on PV components made by Chinese companies. Production of U.S. modules recovered modestly for several years and then began growing substantially in 2019. Manufacturers attributed this growth to a reduction in the corporate tax rate and passage of a tariff on virtually all imported PV modules in 2018. Additional trade barriers over the next several years were joined by a legislative package in 2022, which created incentives for U.S. PV and BESS manufacturers as well as PV and BESS project owners that used domestic products. Domestic module manufacturing continued to grow rapidly.
